claim: CRISPR was originally identified in the immune system of bacteria with the function of destroying invading microphage DNA by enzymatic digestion.
source: Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) was originally identified in the immune system of bacteria, with the function of destroying the invading microphage DNA by enzymatic digestion.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about CRISPR systems in bacteria.

claim: CRISPR has been developed into a highly efficient gene editing tool.
source: The system has been developed into a highly efficient gene editing tool (Doudna and Charpentier, 2014; Mali et al., 2013c)
evidence: Supported by citations to published work by Doudna and Charpentier, 2014 and Mali et al., 2013c.

evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2018.

claim: It is difficult to package most dCas9 fusion proteins into adeno-associated virus (AAV) for in vivo application.
source: However, it is difficult to package most of these dCas9 fusion proteins into adeno-associated virus (AAV) for in vivo application.
evidence: This is a known limitation based on the size constraints of AAV packaging capacity.

claim: Compared with dCas9 engineering, sgRNA is more simple, flexible, and efficient to redesign.
source: Compared with dCas9 engineering, sgRNA is more simple, flexible, and efficient to redesign.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relative complexity of protein versus RNA engineering.

claim: The engineered sgRNA is more helpful for the in vivo application of dCas9-based activators because of its limited length for virus packaging.
source: Moreover, the engineered sgRNA is more helpful for the in vivo application of dCas9-based activators because of its limited length for virus packaging.
evidence: This is an inference based on the size constraints of viral packaging.

claim: The synergistic activation mediator (SAM) system is the most widely used sgRNA-based gene activator, in which MS2 loops are fused to the 3′ end of sgRNA.
source: The most widely used sgRNA-based gene activator is the synergistic activation mediator (SAM) system, in which MS2 loops are fused to the 3′ end of sgRNA (Konermann et al., 2015; Liao et al., 2017).

claim: Pumilio/FBF (PUF), modular scaffold RNAs (MS2, PP7, and com), and riboswitches have been fused to sgRNA.

claim: Chimeric sgRNA-based strategies are limited by their complicated RNA aptamers and the cognate RNA-binding fusion proteins.

claim: Current dCas9-based transcriptional activators are relatively inefficient in endogenous gene activation and cell reprogramming.
source: Although variant dCas9-based activators have been developed (Chen and Qi, 2017), the current dCas9-based transcriptional activators are relatively inefficient in endogenous gene activation and cell reprogramming (Gao et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chen and Qi, 2017 and Gao et al., 2014.

claim: The majority of second-generation activators had higher activity than that of dCas9-VP64 across various cell types and species (human, mouse, and fly).
source: By a systematic comparison of relative potency and effectiveness across various cell types and species (human, mouse, and fly) (Chavez et al., 2016), it was found that the majority of second-generation activators had higher activity than that of dCas9-VP64
evidence: Supported by citation to Chavez et al., 2016.

claim: VPR, SAM, and Suntag are the three most potent dCas9-based activators.
source: By a systematic comparison of relative potency and effectiveness across various cell types and species (human, mouse, and fly) (Chavez et al., 2016), it was found that the majority of second-generation activators had higher activity than that of dCas9-VP64, with the three most potent activators being VPR, SAM, and Suntag.
evidence: Supported by citation to Chavez et al., 2016.

claim: VPR, SAM, and Suntag were consistently better than VP64 across a range of target genes and cellular environments.
source: The three activators were consistently better than VP64 across a range of target genes and cellular environments.
evidence: This is based on the systematic comparison cited from Chavez et al., 2016.

claim: VPR, SAM, and Suntag showed a similar level of activity.
source: Moreover, the three activators showed a similar level of activity
evidence: This is based on the systematic comparison cited from Chavez et al., 2016.

claim: Fusing elements of VPR, SAM, and Suntag did not yield more potent activators.
source: Moreover, the three activators showed a similar level of activity, and fusing their elements did not yield more potent activators (Chavez et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chavez et al., 2016.

claim: Novel, more potent dCas9-based activators might be built by creating other architectures.
source: Novel, more potent dCas9-based activators might be built by creating other architectures.
evidence: This is speculation about future development based on the limitations of current systems.

claim: The human cytomegalovirus (CMV) enhancer/promoter was found almost three decades ago.
source: Almost three decades ago, the human cytomegalovirus (CMV) enhancer/promoter (referred to as CMV enhancer hereafter) was found.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the discovery timeline of the CMV enhancer.

claim: The CMV enhancer is a natural mammalian promoter with high transcriptional activity.
source: Almost three decades ago, the human cytomegalovirus (CMV) enhancer/promoter (referred to as CMV enhancer hereafter) was found. It is a natural mammalian promoter with high transcriptional activity (Boshart et al., 1985).
evidence: Supported by citation to Boshart et al., 1985.

claim: The CMV enhancer is a strong enhancer in various mammalian cells.
source: Later studies showed the CMV enhancer to be a strong enhancer in various mammalian cells (Boshart et al., 1985; Foecking and Hofstetter, 1986; Ho et al., 2015; Kim et al., 1990).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The CMV enhancer has been widely used to drive ectopic expression of various genes in a wide range of mammalian cells.
source: This enhancer has been widely used to drive ectopic expression of various genes in a wide range of mammalian cells
evidence: This is established knowledge about the widespread use of CMV enhancer.

claim: The CMV enhancer has been used to drive ectopic expression of exogenous genes in broad tissues in transgenic animals.

evidence: Supported by citations to Furth et al., 1991 and Schmidt et al., 1990.

claim: The CMV enhancer has been used for protein production by gene engineering and gene therapy.
source: This enhancer has been widely used to drive ectopic expression of various genes in a wide range of mammalian cells, and to drive ectopic expression of exogenous genes in broad tissues in transgenic animals (Furth et al., 1991; Schmidt et al., 1990), protein production by gene engineering, and gene therapy.
evidence: This is established knowledge about applications of CMV enhancer.

claim: The transcriptional activity of the CMV enhancer was recently improved by changing the natural NF-κB binding sites into artificially selected NF-κB binding sequences with high binding affinity.
source: We have recently improved the transcriptional activity of the CMV enhancer by changing the natural NF-κB binding sites into artificially selected NF-κB binding sequences with high binding affinity (Wang et al., 2018).

claim: A capture sgRNA (csgRNA) was produced by adding a capture sequence to the 3′ end of a normal sgRNA sequence.
source: A capture sgRNA (csgRNA) was produced by adding a capture sequence to the 3′ end of a normal sgRNA sequence.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: A linear stick-end CMV (sCMV) enhancer was produced by adding a 3′ end single-strand overhang.
source: A linear stick-end CMV (sCMV) enhancer was produced by adding a 3′ end single-strand overhang.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The overhang of sCMV can anneal with the csgRNA capture sequence.
source: The overhang can anneal with the csgRNA capture sequence.

claim: When dCas9 protein is guided to the promoter of the target gene by csgRNA, sCMV can be recruited by csgRNA.
source: When dCas9 protein was guided to the promoter of the target gene by csgRNA, sCMV could be recruited by csgRNA.

source: The recruited sCMV may activate the transcription of the target gene like a natural looped cis enhancer.

claim: The capture sequence does not affect the function of sgRNA.
source: The results indicated that the target DNA could be digested by all sgRNAs (Figure 1b), indicating that the capture sequence did not affect the sgRNA function.

claim: Three csgRNAs with different capture sequences targeting the same site of the HNF4α promoter can all function to guide Cas9 endonuclease to cut target DNA.

evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.
